max_tire.note: Owners' favorite: as tall as a 285/75R16 but narrower, with less drag and scrub. 34-inch 8.25 tires fit but were too tall for the 2.4 TD's power, and one owner advises against 285s on a 2.4.
Fitted by ATL on its 2.5 TDI trucks, and the size one owner would choose for a 718. There's no established lift market for the swing-axle Turbo D.

timeline.change: Steyr-Daimler-Puch begins developing the second-generation Pinzgauer
716 (4×4) and 718 (6×6) Turbo D enter production in Graz with the VW 2.4 turbo-diesel six, disc brakes and ZF automatic or five-speed manual (sources differ on 1985 or 1986)
Original spec: small nose, no intercooler, cooling versions A and B. Owners say the earlier TDs were known to run hot, and later trucks got a revised cooling system
Revised cooling (versions C and D from chassis 1791) and a larger radiator nose. Later P90s replace the axle-tube O-ring with a plastic ring and sealant
The US Army buys about 20 turbo-diesel 718Ms for special-operations reconnaissance; they're phased out around 2010–11
Intercooled 2.4 TD (owners cite the ACL code) and a new injection pump
Magna sells the Pinzgauer rights to Automotive Technik Ltd; the factory moves to the UK between 2000 and 2002. Austrian chassis numbers run below 6000, UK numbers from 6000
VW 2.5 TDI five-cylinder (BBR) replaces the 2.4 to meet Euro 3, with the automatic only
BAE Systems acquires the business and ends UK production; the planned Pinzgauer II is never built
Ex-US military 718s are sold off as government surplus, giving the US a small batch of domestically sourced Turbo Ds

identify.intro: Pinzgauers were built to order in batches and often updated before delivery, so the badge on the nose doesn't settle much. Work out the revision, the engine and the paperwork before you pay.

items.head: 716/718 vs 710/712
items.body: The Turbo D has a bulged radiator nose, disc brakes and a 5×130 wheel pattern. The petrol 710/712 has a flatter front, drums and a different bolt pattern, and few drivetrain parts interchange.

items.head: P80, P90 or P93
items.body: Look at the nose: the P80 has the smallest radiator cover, and it grew with the P90 and P93. P93s have an intercooler. Some P80s were factory-upgraded to P90 spec; one importer says trucks upgraded outside the factory have cowls cut by hand to clear the radiator hoses.

items.head: VIN
items.body: Pinzgauers use the international 17-digit VIN with the WMI VAG, for example VAG71623110001645 on a 1990 716K. The model number follows the WMI. Position 10 means left-hand drive (1) or right-hand drive (2), not the model year, which confuses US insurers. The last digits are the chassis number.

items.head: Build year
items.body: No model year is stamped on a 716 or 718. The transmission and transfer-case data plates sometimes carry a date (for those parts only). A build certificate from the factory is the only definitive record.

items.head: Ex-US special-ops 718
items.body: US military trucks were P90s or upgraded P80s with lever-action ignition switches; some had a control for a crawler reduction box. Ask for the surplus sale paperwork.

capability.note: Wikipedia, listed under the first generation; check your truck's plate

capability.v: About 11–12 mpg US (2.4 TD); about 15 mpg (ATL 2.5 TDI 718K)

values.intro: Turbo Ds rarely come up for public sale in the US, and the few results cover a wide range: well-built, refurbished trucks now bring far more than the petrol 710s, which trade mostly in the teens on BaT.

paragraphs: Steyr-Daimler-Puch never sold the Turbo D new in the US. The only domestic trucks are the roughly 20 718Ms the US Army bought for special operations, some of which were sold as surplus around 2011. Every other 716 and 718 here is an import, usually ex-military from the UK or elsewhere in Europe.

Under NHTSA's 25-year exemption, every Austrian-built truck (production ended in Graz in 2000) is now eligible, and UK-built ATL trucks become eligible as each reaches 25 years from its build date, so the 2.5 TDI trucks are still mostly too new. Because the VIN carries no model year, use a factory build certificate to prove age.

Federal eligibility doesn't guarantee a plate. A veteran owner notes that each state decides; his 716 was registered in California by mistake and later grandfathered, and owners describe California as the hardest state. In 2022 a Colorado county DMV flagged a Pinzgauer VIN as military and refused it for on-road use, while a 718 bought new from Steyr by a German civilian company was expected to be easier to register. Insurers may balk at the 'abnormal' VIN too.

production.intro: Built to order for military and government customers in Graz, then in the UK; total Turbo D numbers aren't published, though German Wikipedia says more than 30,000 Pinzgauers of all types were built by 2000.

items.v: Graz, Austria (Steyr-Daimler-Puch) to 2000; Guildford, UK (Automotive Technik, later BAE) to about 2007
New Zealand 321 (8 variants); Malaysia 168 716 gun tractors and 164 718 mortar carriers; US Army about 20 718M

editions.name: Pinzgauer Vector
editions.note: Lightly armoured 6×6 protected patrol vehicle for the British Army; withdrawn after problems with suspension, hubs and IED protection

production.paint: UK Pinzgauers were delivered in Austrian army green (RAL 6031), not NATO green, according to a Real 4x4s member involved with the UK trucks.
